name: Abseil Logging
listed_description: The Abseil Logging library provides facilities for writing log messages to stderr, files, or other sinks.
reason: No numeric comparison against any baseline anywhere reachable. absl/log/log_benchmark.cc only measures its own overheads (disabled/enabled LOG, CHECK, VLOG_IS_ON) with no glog, spdlog or std::cerr counterpart; the docs page abseil.io was unreachable (ENOTFOUND). Third-party logging shootouts found (MuggleWei/cc_log_benchmark: easyloggingpp, fmtlog, glog, haclog, loguru, nanolog, quill, reckless, spdlog; spdlog README; RafaGago/logger-bench) do not include absl::log.

name: ArrayFire
reason: Repo README claims only 'Rigorous benchmarks and tests ensuring top performance' and 'near-optimal kernels' with no numbers; docs and release notes (pages/release_notes.md) hold no baseline comparison. The only comparison found is ArrayFire's own 2014-era blog post 'Benchmarking parallel vector libraries' (ArrayFire 3.0 vs Boost.Compute, Bolt, TBB, Thrust on K20, FirePro S10000, Xeon E5-2560v2), which is on arrayfire.com (ENOTFOUND here, never opened) and per search snippets shows mixed results (Thrust faster than ArrayFire on K20 above 1M elements). Directional claim only, no openable numbers.

name: Async++
listed_description: A lightweight concurrency framework for C++11, inspired by the Microsoft PPL library and the N3428 C++ standard proposal.
reason: No benchmark or performance claim in README, wiki (Home, Tasks, Parallel algorithms, Schedulers), issues or repo tree (examples, include, src only). Not included in the tzcnt/runtime-benchmarks shootout (citor, libfork, TooManyCooks, tbb, taskflow, cppcoro, coros, HPX, concurrencpp, libcoro, cobalt); no other shootout naming Async++ was found.

name: Boost.Compute
listed_description: A C++ GPU Computing Library for OpenCL.
reason: Repo has a perf/ directory (perf_stl_*, perf_tbb_*, perf_thrust_*, perf_bolt_* benchmarks) and doc/performance.qbk (Tesla K40c, Core i7 920, gcc -O3), but the results are only embedded as PNG plots (images/perf/*.png) that are not in the checked-out tree (404), and the docs hosting site boostorg.github.io is blocked, so no number could be read. PR threads #266, #353 and #453 carry no timings. The only third-party figures reachable (Merry, arXiv 1601.03144, via search snippet only, not opened) report Boost.Compute as slower than CLOGS/Bolt/VexCL on sort and scan.
